title: fix(fields): a lookup option's label ranks displayField, then nameField, then titleFormat (ADR-0079)
body:
Fixes #10343
Clause-②: no

A lookup option's label now follows the ADR-0079 order the record page follows: the lookup field's own declared `displayField`, then the referenced object's declared `nameField`, then the deprecated `titleFormat`. This is the lookup branch of ruling C1 on objectui#9436 (class-1 ruling comment 5657441402, ratified 5814246926); triage comment 5820783707 placed `displayField` first.

## What changes

`recordToOption` in `packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx` builds every lookup option label. It rendered `titleFormat` first, with the widget's own copy of the template renderer. It now calls `@object-ui/core`'s `getRecordDisplayName(objectDef, row, { titleField: declaredDisplayField })`, the same call `LookupCellRenderer` (`resolveLookupRecordName`) already makes, and stops short of its `Record #id` floor.

| # | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `titleFormat` (the widget's private renderer) | the field's declared `displayField` (the resolver's `titleField` rung) |
| 2 | `displayField`, defaulting to `name` when undeclared | the object's `nameField`, then `displayNameField` |
| 3 | unified resolver: `nameField`, template, derivation, record keys | `titleFormat`, via the shared `formatTitleTemplate` |
| 4 | legacy name list, then the id | type-aware derivation, then name-ish record keys |
| 5 | | the display field on the record (declared, else `name`): the first rung when no schema is available |
| 6 | | legacy name list, then the id |

The widget's private `formatRecordTitle` is deleted. `refTitleFormat` now feeds only `RecordPickerDialog`.

## The guard: `displayField`'s position agrees with the record page

The record page (`ba0b61a`, objectui#10358) ranks an explicit per-view pointer above the declared pointer. `DetailView.resolveDisplayTitle` puts `primaryField` first, and `PageHeaderRenderer` puts an explicit `schema.title` first. Core `getRecordDisplayName` puts `options.titleField` at step 0: "the caller's own DECLARED view-level pointer", which "outranks the object's own pointer by design". The lookup cell passes the declared `displayField` there, pinned by "explicit displayField wins over the schema nameField" in `lookupCellDisplayName.test.tsx`. Triage gives the same answer, so no decision is owed. No record-page logic is copied. The record page reads `declaredNameField` and `recordDisplayValueAt` separately only because it interleaves its own template rendering, and the widget has no template step of its own.

## Why the undeclared `name` default also moves below the object's declarations

Before this PR, three relations held: the template above `nameField`, the template above the `name` default, and the `name` default above `nameField`. The ruling flips the first one, and no order can then keep both of the other two. Keeping "the `name` default above the template" tests red (ablation A1 below). It reddens two existing pins and triage's "only titleFormat" pin. The spec names the default too: `displayField` is the field shown as each candidate's label "(defaults to the referenced object's name/title)". The `LookupFieldMetadata.displayField` doc says it "Falls back to `reference_field`, then the referenced object's own display-name resolution, then the raw id". So when a schema is present, the guess sits below the object's declarations. Without a schema, the label still reads `name` first, on the same code path as before.

## Callers

All nine call sites go through `recordToOption`: popover candidates, recents, the three hydration branches, the expanded-reference selected value (`resolveSelectedOption`), picker-selected records (`handlePickerSelectRecords`), and both quick-create paths. The selected chip has no resolver of its own. It renders `option.label`. In the dependency arrays, `refTitleFormat` is removed where nothing reads it any more, and `handlePickerSelectRecords` now lists `refObjectSchema`, which it read without listing. Before this PR, its `refTitleFormat` entry refreshed it only when the schema carried a template.

## Pins: `LookupField.labelOrder-10343.test.tsx`

On the base `ab50ccc`, with `LookupField.tsx` byte-equal to the base: 4 failed, 2 passed. At head `600c330`: 6 passed. The base run used the same assertions. The later fixture change only swapped `any` for `unknown`.

| Pin | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| object declares `nameField` + `titleFormat` ⇒ `HT-001` | red, got `Globex / HT-001` | green |
| field declares `displayField: short_code` ⇒ `AC` | red, got `Globex / HT-001` | green |
| only `titleFormat` ⇒ the template | green | green |
| control: `nameField` blank on the record ⇒ the template | green | green |
| control: a `{{field}}` template renders as `{field}` | red, got `{Globex} / {HT-001}` | green |
| the selected chip of an expanded reference ⇒ `HT-001` | red, chip `Globex / HT-001` | green |

Every fixture record also carries a `name` value, so a `name`-first order cannot pass.

## Ablations (one-shot, at `7ce2686`)

Each ablation ran through `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor had to hit exactly once, and the tool proved each mutation on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed). It then restored the file and proved it (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The test imports `./LookupField`, and vitest aliases `@object-ui/core` to `packages/core/src`, so no `dist` was involved.

- **A1**, the `name` guess above the resolver: `unified ??` moved below `shown[displayField ?? DEFAULT_DISPLAY_FIELD] ??`. Predicted red: pin 1, pin 3, both template controls, the chip, and two existing pins. Pin 2 was predicted green. Observed across three files: 7 failed, 20 passed, exactly that set. The existing pins were "control: with no policy loaded, the same `titleFormat` renders every field it names" (`LookupField.displayFls-10373.test.tsx`) and "dropdown: same labels, same subtitles, same record handed to onSelectRecord" (`LookupField.candidateExpand-10223.test.tsx`).
- **A2**, the declared `displayField` rung dropped: `{ titleField: displayField }` removed. Predicted red: pin 2 only. Observed: 1 failed, 5 passed, with `expected [ 'HT-001', 'HT-002' ] to deeply equal [ 'AC', 'IN' ]`.

## Verification at `600c330` (final head)

- `turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/fields^..." --concurrency=2`: 10 of 10 successful (cached).
- `@object-ui/fields` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFiles` confirms the new test is inside the test program.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --shard=N/4 packages/fields/` from the repo root, all four shards: 47 + 47 + 47 + 46 = 187 files, the package's tracked test-file count. 3101 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed.
- `check-changeset-presence`: 2 source files of 1 released package, 1 changeset. `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-changeset-overwrite`: OK. `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new. `check:control-bytes`: OK. `check-pending-changeset-literals` and `check-changeset-claims`: OK. `check-test-path-roots` and the three `check-vi-mock-*` gates: OK.
- ESLint, narrowed to the two changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 0 errors.
  - Population: eslint's own config (`ESLint.isPathIgnored` is false for 2 of 2).
  - File count, read from `--format json`: 2.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` extends `tseslint.configs.recommended`, which is not type-checked, and sets no `parserOptions` or `projectService`. None of the 23 files under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem (a grep for fs reads found 0 matches; the same grep matches `scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` as a control). So this diff cannot change a verdict on an untouched file.
  - Per rule against the base, on `LookupField.tsx`: `no-explicit-any` 41 to 39, `exhaustive-deps` 4 to 3, the rest unchanged. The new test file has 2 `no-explicit-any` warnings, from the data-source casts the sibling tests use too.
- NOT MEASURED: repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test`. CI runs both.

## Acceptance notes

- **The browse-all picker's display column still renders the template first.** `renderLookupColumnValue` (`lookupColumnDisplay.tsx`, used by `RecordPickerDialog`) renders `titleFormat` for the display column, above that column's own value and the object's `nameField`. It also leaves a `{{field}}` template's braces in place. A temporary probe (not committed) measured this at this head:
  - An object with `nameField: contract_no` and `titleFormat: '{party} / {contract_no}'`: the dropdown shows `["HT-001"]`, but the picker's `name` column shows `Globex / HT-001`.
  - `{{party}} / {{contract_no}}`: the picker shows `{Globex} / {HT-001}`.
  - Before this PR both surfaces showed the template. On such an object they now read differently until that renderer changes too.
  - Left untouched here: it is outside the file surface, and what the display column should show is a design choice, not a mechanical change. Reported for the seat to card. The changeset says the column is unchanged.
- **A bare-id value hydrated on mount is labelled without the referenced object's schema.** The hydration effect captures `refObjectSchema` before `getObjectSchema` resolves. Its dependency list is eslint-disabled and does not re-run it. Probe at this head: value `c1`, object `nameField: contract_no`. The chip reads `Acme` (the record's `name`), while the dropdown reads `HT-001`, and the lookup cell resolves a bare id through the schema's `nameField` (its pin "fetch-on-demand primitive id resolves via the schema nameField too"). The base passes the same null schema on this path. That is a code reading; the probe did not run on the base. This PR does not change it. Reported.
- The changeset declares `'@object-ui/fields': patch`, as dispatched. The objectui#9436 changesets declared `minor` for their behaviour change.
